The *Adhikaraṇavāra* (Pvr 2.6) is an analytical section of the *Parivāra*, the concluding book of the Pali *Vinaya Piṭaka* [SuttaCentral]. Rendered as "The legal issues to which each offense belongs," the text provides a systematic scholastic classification that relates the various Vinaya disciplinary rules to the four categories of monastic legal procedures (*adhikaraṇa*) [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the text has been made available by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

No external parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections are reported by SuttaCentral or attested with significant scores in DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies 65 matching passages across 13 texts, demonstrating dense internal reuse across the *Parivāra* [DharmaNexus]. In particular, the section shares significant passages with corresponding chapters addressing legal questions elsewhere in the collection, notably the *Adhikaraṇavāra* of Pvr 1.6 (sharing up to §0.1–3.1) and Pvr 1.14 (§1.1–3.1), as well as Pvr 2.14 [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits widespread formulaic reuse with adjacent analytical chapters in the second division of the *Parivāra*—including the *Samuṭṭhānavāra* (Pvr 2.5), *Vipattivāra* (Pvr 2.3), *Samuccayavāra* (Pvr 2.8), *Samathavāra* (Pvr 2.7), and *Katāpattivāra* (Pvr 2.2)—as well as topical treatises on legal disputes such as the *Samathabheda* (Pvr 5) and *Adhikaraṇabheda* (Pvr 11) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond the *Parivāra*, minor segment alignment is detected with the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Bi-Vb Pj 5) [DharmaNexus].
